**Title (English, from literature):** Lying on the same bed

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

**Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 31** (*Ekamañcatuvaṭṭana*, "Lying on the same bed") is a Vinaya rule stipulating an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) for a nun who lies down on the same bed with another nun. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali. According to the non-offense (*anāpatti*) clause in the canonical text (Vin IV 289), it is permissible to share a bed if a boundary or separation (*vavatthāna*) is established [Hüsken 1997]. The commentary *Samantapāsādikā* (Sp 932) clarifies that this separation can be designated by placing a monastic robe (*kāsāva*), a staff, or even a waistband (*kāyabandhana*) between the two nuns [Hüsken 1997]. In modern scholarship, Ernst Waldschmidt and others classify Pācittiya 31 alongside Pācittiya 32 as regulations concerning sexual conduct [Hüsken 1997].
